messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: [irace-package] debug level: details?
parts:
On 14/08/17 08:11, M. Wagner wrote:
> How many levels are there? Due to my short attention span, I simply set the level to 10 ;)

I just checked the sources and right now the higher value tested is 3, so
higher values are the same as 3. However, this option is for debugging
purposes, so higher values may appear or messages may move to higher/lower values.

>> If you have suggestions about how to structure the levels and what to print at each level (or any extra info that could be useful), please let us know.
>
> Oh, I’d love to suggest something, but I ain’t no software engineer by trade.
>
> You are mentioning in the manual what 0 does, but not what >0 does. A very rough, incremental outline might still be useful (e.g., at level 1 XYZ gets printed as well, at level 2 ABC,

It would be a very long list that would need to be maintained carefully. What
we have done so far is that every time, we needed to print something to debug
irace, we kept the code but place it under --debug-level. If the message is
short and relatively infrequent, we keep it at 1. If it adds a lot to the
output, we place it at higher levels.

Ideally, you should not need to use any debug-level to understand what irace is
doing, unless something goes wrong. In fact, I feel that irace is a bit too
verbose even at --debug-level 0, but it may be just a matter of taste.

Cheers,

Manuel.
